source: Hoegaarden Hall of Records · Chronicles of Aleforge, vol. XXII
title: Of the Long Thirst
paragraphs: In the Year 412, Scipium Ofkra, born in Aleforge but schooled in Providence and pious as any priest of Patmos, spent his last act as Liquor King abolishing the Drunken Trials. With no Trials there could be no new King, and so began what the taverns have named the Long Thirst.

Aleforge has since been left to its mayors. Cromwell kept the chair from 412 to 425, and was found more often in the brothels than in the hall. Bronco Chestnut, a son of the Church of Patmos, sought to make the city holier still and was turned out within two years. Glendolph Galleyway has held the seat since 427, and of him the record has little to say.
Isadora Beerchelli foretold this drought long before it came. The drinkers of the Isles quote her yet, and they wait.
signoff: Set down in the Hall of Records, Year 448.
